thread:
ops-bot: ALERT: sustained spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 and us-central-1. error_rate 5xx > 7% for 3m, p95 latency up from 120ms to 2.3s. auto-escalating to #incidents :rotating_light:

mary-oncall: ack I'm awake and taking pager. tagging infra and runtime. switching phone to DND off.

kevin-infra: on call. pulling metrics now. can someone post sample request ids?

ashley-ml: I have a few request_ids from Kibana: req_20260315_8f9, req_20260315_b21, req_20260315_c73. most show timeouts inside batching scheduler (wait_for_batch queued > 120s).

jordan-platform: confirmed, our internal batching queue length spiked ~30k across scheduler instances. looks like head-of-line blocking in the batcher where a few large seq requests are preventing flush.

ops-bot: paging mary-oncall and kevin-infra. escalation policy: notify SRE lead in 5m if not acked.

mary-oncall: oncall handoff: i'll coordinate. kevin, can you check active batcher worker counts and if autoscale throttled?

kevin-infra: fetching autoscale events...

kevin-infra: autoscaler did not trigger because pod CPU < target due to GPU-bound work. batcher backlog metrics show per-shard queue length skyrocketed. worker_counts: desired 12, ready 10, busy 10. recent deploy at 03:05 increased tokenization CPU; suspect throttling at gateway + batcher coupling.

ashley-ml: hypothesis: a small fraction of long context requests (len>64k tokens) are causing large KV caches and very long service times, holding the batch open until timeout.

mary-oncall: mitigation plan options: 1) temporarily disable batching for critical routes, 2) enable per-request max-batch-size override, 3) route traffic to fallback lighter-weight model variant, 4) evict oldest queued requests preemptively. Thoughts?

jordan-platform: quick wins: route critical customers to fallback model variant (lower latency) + enable eviction policy. disabling batching will increase GPU cost but decrease HOL and 5xx.

kevin-infra: I can flip routing and update rollout to fall back to model:a10-lite in eu-west-1 for high-error customers. doing a canary redirect 5% first.

kevin-infra: command I will run:
```bash
# update routing policy for customer tier 'paid'
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west-1 --selector "customer_tier=paid" --fallback-model a10-lite --weight 5
```

kevin-infra: executed canary redirect at 03:18. monitoring errors.

mary-oncall: parallel: enable eviction to drop longest-waiting 10% of queued requests to free head-of-line. jordan, can you apply eviction config on batcher?

jordan-platform: applying eviction config now. patch:
```yaml
batcher: 
  eviction_policy: longest_wait
  eviction_threshold_pct: 10
  eviction_interval_s: 30
```
applied to runtime cluster eu-west-1 at 03:20.

ops-bot: NOTE: A/B config change recorded: rollout id rtr-20260315-001.

ashley-ml: after eviction and canary routing p95 dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s in the canary subset. overall 5xx reduced to ~3.2% and trending down.

kevin-infra: increasing batcher replicas by 3 to handle load; command:
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/batcher --replicas=13 -n runtime-eu-west-1
```
scale started at 03:25.

mary-oncall: monitoring customer impact. Sam (cs), Leo (support) are you seeing increased tickets or customer-visible errors?

sam-cs: leo-support and I see spikes in error reports, mostly timeouts from integrations using streaming. we've pushed an advisory to customers: "we're mitigating elevated errors, temporary degraded latency for some large requests".

leo-support: CS note: top impacted customers: AcmeCorp (high), NovaApps (medium). CS will accept routing to fallback and offer to replay failed requests if desired.

kevin-infra: replicas up to 13, new pods coming up 03:27. readiness_ok on 2/3 so far. memory pressure low.

mary-oncall: good. let's keep canary at 5% for 4m then ramp to 50% if stable. jordan, leave eviction in place for now. ashley, can you run quick eval on sample long-ctx requests to see if we can reject upfront?

ashley-ml: running prompt-length heuristic check now. we can add a lightweight reject at ingress for requests > 40k tokens returning 4xx with guidance. Draft rule:
```json
{"max_tokens":40000, "response":"request exceeds supported context length for this tier; please use streaming or batch processing"}
```
I can ship this as a patch to the gateway in 10m.

ops-bot: incident timeline: detection 03:12 -> canary routing + eviction 03:18-03:20 -> scale 03:25 -> tail latency improving 03:28. continue monitoring.

mary-oncall: current customer impact: partial (some requests failing, fallbacks mitigating major customers). severity: Sev2. action items: 1) keep eviction + canary routing, 2) ramp fallback to 50% in 8m if green, 3) enable ingress length checks, 4) prepare postmortem with root cause on long requests + batching coupling. assign owners: kevin (routing/scale), jordan (eviction/config), ashley (ingress heuristic + eval), sam (customer comms), mary (incident lead).

kevin-infra: will ramp fallback to 50% at 03:36 if canary remains stable.

jordan-platform: will keep eviction live and add metrics to track evicted count / sec.

ashley-ml: will open PR for gateway reject rule (target merge in 10m) and run regression against samples.

sam-cs: updated customers with status and ETA. offering to replay where appropriate.

mary-oncall: great. any signs of secondary failures or region spillover?

kevin-infra: us-central-1 also saw similar pattern but lower magnitude; applying same minimal eviction + fallback there as well (rolling).

ops-bot: ALERT: 95th percentile across platform reduced to 720ms, 5xx now 1.1% (down from 7%). continuing to watch for 15m.

leo-support: customers reporting fewer errors now. ticket volume stabilizing.

mary-oncall: marking as "mitigated" at 03:45 but remain on-call for next 60m. will convene post-incident review in 48h. please capture logs, sample long requests, and deploy timelines.

kevin-infra: capturing autoscaler logs; attaching cluster events to the incident doc.

jordan-platform: saving batcher traces and eviction metrics to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/20260315/1716804321/

ashley-ml: I'll evaluate whether to add model-side per-request timeouts to reduce HOL risk.

mary-oncall: thanks team. final note: short-term mitigations: eviction + fallback + ingress checks. long-term: better long-request handling, admission controls, and autoscale aware of GPU utilization. we'll capture next steps in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
